results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 37 body and conclusion units of the reverse outline state the controlling idea of the spec paragraph they are aligned to (p01-p38 in order); the three opening callouts are page format and match no spec paragraph. The outline's extra clause on Dysfunctions ¶2 (Corvane's hiring wave as Hamster Wheel plus Ivory Tower) is a second instance of p14's mapping, not a different idea.

The outliner marked four units as holding two ideas; none is a failure. Introduction ¶2 (claim and roadmap) is what p02's controlling idea itself contains; Pattern ¶2 (is the problem structural / ask about the work) are the two halves of p16's single idea, discovery; What to Take Away ¶3 carries p36 plus the conclusion's synthesis sentence as a second bullet of one labelled list; Checklist ¶2 carries the callback and the hand-off, which the page format places in the closing paragraph.
Every unit serves the supporting claim its section declares (S1 rings, S2 output/outcome and the scene, S3 dysfunctions, S4 pattern, brief, worked example and AI, S5 limits); no unit is off-thesis.

results.quote: he calls accidentally missing someone "the cardinal sin of reorganization"
results.finding: The quotation is given without saying what 'missing someone' means or how it shows the cost of repeated change, which is what the sentence offers it for (spec p23: 'the anchor treats the cost of change to people as a first-order constraint'). Both flow readers stopped at it (A item 15, B item 15: 'Missing someone how?'; 'a different cost from change fatigue'). All other evidence items, the six tables, Figure 1 and the Perri quotations are introduced and interpreted.
results.waived_by: Author (Željko Obrenović), 2026-11-19, rule 'max two rounds per chapter': the unit was revised after round 2 to address this finding and was not re-checked by fresh readers.

results.quote: That speed has a possible effect on the brief itself.
results.finding: The declared relationship is cause_effect from 'work inside teams changing quickly' to the measures a brief uses. 'That speed' points at the speed with which teams change their way of working (¶1), but the cause the paragraph then argues from is a different speed, 'If producing a change takes less time'. The causal link is asserted by the pronoun and not made; both flow readers reported that the link does not hold (A item 21, B item 21: 're-read twice'). A bridging clause that agents shorten the time to produce a change would make it. The spec's carries_over is itself loose on this point, but the draft can express the relationship without a spec change. All other 34 transitions express their declared relationship at the boundary.
results.waived_by: Author (Željko Obrenović), 2026-11-19, rule 'max two rounds per chapter': the unit was revised after round 2 to address this finding and was not re-checked by fresh readers.

results.finding: The introduction opens on a concrete puzzling scenario (Corvane's finished and unjudgeable reorganization), bridges from the reader's own practice, and states claim and roadmap; no dictionary definition, sweeping generalisation, restated title or announcement-only opening.

The conclusion sorts its claims by how settled they are, states the author's synthesis, gives a course of action (the checklist) and returns to the opening case; it is not a bare summary, introduces no new argument and does not apologise or trail off.

Synthesis and so-what are both present: the means/end synthesis in What to Take Away ¶3, and the so-what in the checklist's instruction ('before any structure is drawn and before anything is announced') and the closing paragraph.
results.quote: The four levers are the means and the users' outcomes are the end. A change that names a lever without a user and an outcome is output.

results.finding: The closing paragraph returns to the board's question from the hook and answers why nobody could answer it.
results.quote: Corvane's board asked whether the hiring wave had worked, and nobody could answer. You can now say why: the plan named a structure and a date, and it named no user and no outcome.

results.finding: The cold reader predicted, from the introduction alone, the eight-part order the body follows (users, output and outcome, dysfunctions, five steps, brief, limits, Corvane again, AI), the central claim, and the Corvane case with its numbers; every roadmap promise is kept in the section the spec names. The reader's four 'unclear' notes are about wording in the lead (e.g. 'both'), not about a section it could not place.

The cold reader, using only the chapter, named the users in three rings (the QA engineers, the product teams that would depend on the team, customers), restated the announcement as an output with no user, measure, baseline, target or date, proposed an outcome measured by customer-found defects per release with a watch on QA wait time, and proposed a smaller test (one or two QA people with one product team for a quarter, announced as a test, reversible, with a failure criterion and review). This meets the expected answer on all three parts.

The chapter states where an organization differs from a product in a three-row table with a 'What changes in the method' column, and says what must not be carried over: cheap withdrawable tests, open research on decisions about individuals, and handing the decision to users.
results.quote: | A test can be shown to a sample and withdrawn | A test changes someone's team, manager or on-call duty, and some changes cannot be undone | Fewer, longer tests; prefer reversible ones; say in advance that it is a test and what happens after |

results.finding: Each concept taken from Build What Matters names the book or its authors, is paraphrased (only the two-word term 'metric of progress' is quoted), and its application to the organization is marked as the author's: key customer/business outcome ('is my extension, not their claim'), key outcome ('which again is my extension of their idea'), the dysfunctions ('The left two columns are theirs; the right column is mine'), vision and the roadmap working backward from it ('which is my extension of their method'), and again in the conclusion and Sources. 'Balanced roadmap' is not used in the chapter, so there is nothing to attribute.
results.quote: Applying that distinction to the organization itself is my extension, not their claim: the owners are served when the three rings are.

results.finding: User, outcome and discovery each get a one-sentence working definition at first substantive use: 'A **user** of an organizational design is anyone whose work the design makes easier or harder'; 'An outcome of an organizational change is a change in what its users can do, stated before the change, with one measure and a date'; 'The first step is **discovery**: finding out what the problem is, from the people in the flow, before choosing a structure.' The separate finding that the rings are not said to be relative to the structure being changed is scored under flow_is_followable; it concerns the rings, not the definition of user.
results.quote: An outcome of an organizational change is a change in what its users can do, stated before the change, with one measure and a date.
